result.question: We filtered the oil on Transformer 1 at site MAIN in early January, and I need a clean pre-filtration baseline to compare against. Pull the hydrogen, methane, ethylene, acetylene and co readings for every oil sample taken in the two months before 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000. Give me the min, max and mean of each gas over that pre-January period, and the average daily rise in ppm/day for hydrogen and acetylene. Then tell me by what percentage each gas is lower in the latest sample than in that baseline, so I can judge how much the filtration is masking the fault gases.
result.answer:
I can't build the baseline you asked for, because there are no readings from before 2024-01-15 in the data. Transformer 1 at MAIN has only 5 records in total, one per day from 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19. There is nothing in the two months before 2024-01-15 (about 2023-11-15 to 2024-01-14). The earliest record is timestamped exactly 2024-01-15T00:00:00, which falls outside a window that ends before that time.

That means I can't give you the pre-filtration min, max and mean, the hydrogen and acetylene ppm/day rise, or the percentage drop against a baseline. Any numbers I gave for those would be invented.

Here is everything the record holds, for reference. All values are in ppm, and every sample was taken after the early-January filtration:

| Date | H₂ | CH₄ | C₂H₄ | C₂H₂ | CO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-15 | 2845 | 7406 | 16684 | 7 | 32 |
| 2024-01-16 | 2950 | 7200 | 16500 | 6 | 30 |
| 2024-01-17 | 2800 | 7300 | 16700 | 8 | 35 |
| 2024-01-18 | 2900 | 7350 | 16600 | 7 | 33 |
| 2024-01-19 (latest) | 2850 | 7400 | 16650 | 7 | 32 |

Even after filtration, hydrogen (about 2,800–2,950), methane (about 7,200–7,400) and ethylene (about 16,500–16,700) are still very high. That points to an active thermal fault, and filtration hasn't removed it.

To do the comparison, you'll need the pre-filtration lab reports or the oil-sampling records (LIMS or the DGA vendor) loaded into the system for Transformer 1. Once that data is in, I can run the baseline statistics, the ppm/day rise and the percentage drop.
